story: Attacks flew straight from the gun, and after just a few kilometres four riders broke clear. Soudal Quick-Step controlled the peloton behind, shutting down any attempts to bridge across. The break’s lead reached three minutes before settling at around two, and although the gap gradually came down on the local circuit, the twisty roads through Milan and the high speed made the chase increasingly difficult. In the finale, Bais sacrificed himself for teammate Maestri, but Dversnes had the stronger sprint, taking victory ahead of Maestri and Marcelussi after a short but intense stage.
